subject: Urban Planning
title: Phoenix: A City That Shouldn't Exist?
description: A micro-lesson that makes Phoenix: A City That Shouldn't Exist? usable.

hook.text: Phoenix, Arizona gets 8 inches of rain per year. Five million people live there. They use Colorado River water.

buildup.text: The Central Arizona Project canal carries water 336 miles uphill from the Colorado River. It's an engineering marvel.

discovery.text: Lake Mead — Phoenix's primary reservoir — has dropped to 30% capacity. The water supply is not guaranteed.

twist.text: Golf courses, lawns, and swimming pools consume vast amounts. Meanwhile, farms use 70% of the state's water.

climax.text: Arizona halted new housing developments in 2023 due to insufficient groundwater. Growth may be over.

punchline.text: Five million people in a desert. The river is running out.

quiz.question: Why did Arizona halt new housing developments in 2023?
options: A recession reduced demand for new homes
Insufficient groundwater to sustain further growth
Federal environmental regulations banned desert construction
